business_problem: Wells Fargo needed to modernize a mainframe-backed card-payment environment so it could scale with rising transaction volumes, reduce dependency on third parties, and deliver a seamless multichannel customer experience.
solution_summary: Wells Fargo launched its Cards 2.0 initiative by building an operational data store on MongoDB after modernizing the legacy mainframe environment behind card payments. External-vendor data still enters the mainframe, but it is pulled into MongoDB Enterprise Advanced and exposed through a façade layer and reusable APIs that feed more than 80 headless microservices across rewards, loyalty, and other payment services. The ODS gives Wells Fargo a sub-second service layer capable of handling more than seven million transactions while curated data products make authenticated information available to downstream processes without forcing teams back into monolithic integrations. By separating systems of record from a flexible operational data layer, the bank can roll out changes across channels faster, reduce third-party dependence, and use transaction data more effectively to personalize customer experiences.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Enterprise Advanced
solution_components.role: Runs the operational data store that exposes mainframe and external-vendor payment data to APIs and microservices.

data_flow: External-vendor data enters the mainframe, is pulled into MongoDB's operational data store, exposed through a façade layer and APIs, and then consumed by headless microservices and curated data products that serve card-payment channels such as rewards and loyalty.
business_outcome: Wells Fargo accelerated feature rollout across channels, improved resiliency for card-payment services, and created a scalable operational data layer that better supports personalized financial experiences.
